text: not a markedly different survival rate.13 The standard combination of drugs consists of daily mercaptopurine and weekly methotrexate.2 Many protocols provide for periods of re-induction therapy (re- peating induction therapy),2 and such intensive therapy is associated with an absolute improvement of about 4% in long-term survival.13 It has been suggested that individual- isation of methotrexate dosage to take account of the pa- tient’s ability to clear the drug can improve the outcome.14 It is generally agreed that patients who maintain remission for 4 years after the end of maintenance therapy are at little risk of relapse and may be regarded as effectively cured. Patients who relapse after stopping treatment can usually be brought to second remission, often by a repeat of their original induction therapy. However, if relapse occurs dur- ing treatment the prognosis is poor, and chemotherapy is unlikely to bring lasting benefit. However, clofarabine monotherapy can induce remission in some children with refractory or relapsed ALL.15 Newer drugs that have been investigated with promising initial results include nelarab- ine, sphingosomal vincristine, and novel BCR-ABL inhib- itors.1 The role of stem cell transplantation (p.1811) in the treat- ment of ALL is a matter of some controversy. Compari- sons between transplantation and intensive chemotherapy have yielded inconsistent results.2 Consequently, alloge- neic transplantation is usually reserved for high-risk pa- tients such as those who do not have a complete remission with induction therapy, and those with Philadelphia-posi- tive ALL (who remain at high-risk even when treated with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor).2 The lack of suitable HLA- matched family donors has led to the investigation of au- tologous purged marrow, or the use of marrow from mis- matched family donors; however, generally neither of these options has proved more effective than chemothera- py.16 Studies suggest that matched unrelated donors or cord-blood transplantation have results comparable with those obtained with matched related donors.2 1.
